reasoning:
All factual claims verified against source. The NRT leak guard at irr.py:372-377 checks alloc_delta != free_delta across the three test runs. All three datasets are tiny (12, 18, 1 rows), so DuckDB has no reason to create multiple partial states per group and almost certainly never calls _irr_combine_impl (lines 170-190). The combine path is therefore unexercised by the guard.

The inlining-dependent refcount claim is technically sound. _irr_combine_impl has signature void(intp, intp, intp, uint64) — no NRT-tracked types — so removerefctpass would strip its NRT ops if the function's LLVM module contains no NRT_MemInfo_alloc* symbol. vector_extend (vector.py:137) calls numpy.empty() and thus brings NRT_MemInfo_alloc* into any function it is inlined into, which disables the pass and keeps the borrow incref + scope-exit decref symmetric (net 0). But test_ducklib.md:155 explicitly documents the asymmetric-stripping failure mode: '@njit wrapper is a separate compilation unit whose LLVM module has no NRT_MemInfo_alloc* — removerefctpass runs there and strips the incref, while the scope-exit decref in the allocating function survives.' The mirror of that risk applies here: if vector_extend is not inlined, _irr_combine_impl has no NRT_MemInfo_alloc*, the pass runs and strips its scope-exit decrefs for src/tgt, while the increfs inside borrow_structref (which returns an NRT-tracked StructRef, so removerefctpass is disabled in that compilation unit) survive — yielding +1 refct per merged state pair. udaf.md section 8 point 1 names this exact risk.

Severity low is correct: this is a test-coverage gap in an example file, the underlying code is likely correct in practice (Numba at default O2 typically inlines vector_extend), and the latent refcount leak would only manifest under parallel DuckDB aggregation that triggers combine — which the existing guard cannot reach. No severity change warranted.
